method: Read the complete current client and checked its new draft-binding/release-gate/request-receipt changes against the previously reviewed source. Verified final client/watchdog/queue and metadata hashes. No credential or local execution-receipt contents were accessed, and no client, test or network operation was executed by this reviewer.
findings: The only newly reachable action is GET of one selected draft's status. Before credential loading, the supplied identifier must match a successful create-draft response receipt for the same selected paper and the exact current canonical metadata and POST-body hashes. The identifier is restricted to the bounded component grammar, and the target remains the fixed official HTTPS submission origin with no redirects or environmental proxy use.

The first successful legacy receipt can be used for this read-only draft association without inventing an upload/file association. The existing independent runtime release-manifest/source/PDF checks still run before the association and request. The GET carries no metadata or file payload and performs no source mutation.

New intent and response records share a fresh request identifier and record the exact file-manifest fingerprint. The first legacy response is not rewritten. Token redaction in keys/values, owner-only atomic local receipts, generic exceptions and no automatic retry remain unchanged.

The hard release gate still refuses create-upload, put-part, complete-upload, source-check, preview, preview-status and commit before credential access. Their dormant implementation is not approved by this delta. Upload association, revision-specific preview validation and unknown-commit outcome handling remain prerequisites to their separate release.

The publication watchdog and its one-path allowlist delta are unchanged. The user already authorized the selected submission workflow and declarations; this read-only schema/status step introduces no new permission request or scheduling/publication claim.
